question: What is a referral in the context of family planning?

options.A: Directing a client to another facility when needs exceed current capacity
options.B: Ordering a new brand of oral contraceptive pills from the pharmacy
options.C: Discharging a client completely from the healthcare system
options.D: Scheduling a routine return visit for the same clinic next month

explanation: A referral happens when a client needs specialized care or resources that the current primary facility cannot provide. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h1)

question: Why is a functional referral system necessary for family planning clients?

options.A: It ensures safe, continuous care when a client needs specialized services
options.B: It allows primary health centers to perform major surgical sterilizations
options.C: It guarantees that clients never have to pay for their contraceptive drugs
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to provide health education at primary clinics

explanation: Referrals link primary care clinics to advanced facilities, ensuring clients get appropriate treatment without dropping out of care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h1)

question: What is a main purpose of a family planning referral?

options.A: To permanently punish clients who miss their clinic appointments
options.B: To reduce the total number of people using modern contraceptives
options.C: To transfer financial responsibility for drugs to the client
options.D: To connect clients with specialized care when needed

explanation: Referrals are primarily designed to link clients to the specific level of care required for their health status. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h2)

question: How do referrals help optimize healthcare resources?

options.A: By stopping the purchase of expensive family planning commodities altogether
options.B: By ensuring that nurses only work one day a week at each health facility
options.C: By forcing all clients to bypass primary centers and go straight to teaching hospitals
options.D: By keeping primary clinics focused on routine care while advanced centers handle complex cases

explanation: Proper referral sorting ensures facilities use their specific staff skills and equipment efficiently without overloading primary centers. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h2)

question: Which facility type represents the primary level of healthcare delivery?
explanation: Primary health care centres and health posts form the grassroots level where basic family planning services are first accessed. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h3)

question: Where should a nurse refer a client who requests a permanent surgical contraceptive method like bilateral tubal ligation?

options.A: To a secondary or tertiary hospital
options.B: To a local patent medicine vendor
options.D: To a community outreach market stall

explanation: Surgical procedures require operating theater facilities and specialized personnel usually found at secondary or tertiary hospitals. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h3)

question: Which client situation is a clear indication for a family planning referral?

options.A: A routine request for a three-month supply of injectable contraceptives
options.B: A first-time visit for condom distribution at a primary clinic
options.C: A simple request for general counseling on reproductive anatomy
options.D: A desire for a permanent surgical method like a vasectomy

explanation: Permanent surgical methods require specialized surgical skills not routinely offered at basic primary care posts. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h4)

question: A client using a combined oral contraceptive pill develops severe throbbing headaches and high blood pressure. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Advise her to stop the pills immediately and refer her to a higher facility for evaluation
options.B: Switch her immediately to an implant at the same primary health post
options.C: Double her dose of oral contraceptive pills to balance her hormone levels
options.D: Reassure the client that headaches are normal and tell her to buy paracetamol

explanation: Severe migraines and high blood pressure are serious warning signs (MEC category 4) requiring prompt discontinuation and medical evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h4)

question: What vital document must a nurse provide when sending a client to another facility?

options.A: A receipt for the purchase of family planning drugs
options.B: A discharge certificate from the local government
options.C: A blank prescription sheet signed by the patient
options.D: A completed and legible referral form

explanation: A formal referral form communicates the clinical history and reason for transfer directly to the receiving healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h5)

question: Why is proper documentation of a referral important for the client's care?

options.A: It proves to the government that the nurse worked extra hours
options.B: It prevents the receiving facility from repeating unnecessary assessments
options.C: It allows the nurse to charge extra administrative fees to the client
options.D: It stops the client from ever returning to the primary health center

explanation: Clear notes on clinical history and vital signs save time and guide the receiving team straight to appropriate management. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h5)

question: What is a primary responsibility of the nurse when initiating a referral?

options.A: Transporting the client personally in her private vehicle
options.B: Performing major surgeries before sending the client away
options.C: Preparing the client emotionally and explaining the reason for referral
options.D: Purchasing the client's transport fare out of her own pocket

explanation: Nurses must counsel clients so they understand why a referral is necessary and feel less anxious about visiting a new facility. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h6)

question: When handling an emergency family planning complication, what extra communication duty does the nurse have?

options.A: Instructing the client to keep all information a secret
options.B: Posting the client's medical details on social media for donations
options.C: Calling or notifying the receiving facility in advance
options.D: Waiting for three days before writing the referral note

explanation: For urgent cases, advance communication ensures the receiving team prepares emergency equipment and bed space before arrival. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h6)

question: Which of the following is a common barrier to effective family planning referrals in Nigeria?

options.A: Short waiting times at all tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: Financial constraints and inability to afford transport costs
options.C: Immediate feedback letters arriving within five minutes
options.D: Excessive availability of free transport services for all clients

explanation: Poverty and transport costs prevent many clients from reaching distant secondary or tertiary referral centers. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h7)

question: What is a major consequence of missing feedback letters from the receiving facility?

options.A: The client automatically becomes pregnant within one week
options.B: The primary clinic is forced to close down permanently
options.C: The primary nurse remains unaware of whether the client received care
options.D: The nurse receives a financial bonus from the government

explanation: Without feedback loops, primary nurses cannot track client outcomes or ensure continuity of community-level care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h7)

question: What is one effective strategy to ensure two-way communication in a referral system?

options.A: Banning clients from ever returning to their original health post
options.B: Using standardized feedback forms sent back by the receiving facility
options.C: Destroying all medical records once a client leaves the primary clinic
options.D: Stopping all phone calls between hospitals and primary centers

explanation: Two-way feedback forms allow receiving hospitals to report back to the referring nurse on the client's outcome. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h8)

question: A nurse notices that many clients referred for long-acting methods never arrive at the general hospital. What practical step can she take to improve follow-up?

options.A: Increase the price of family planning commodities at her clinic
options.B: Scold clients publicly during clinic meetings for failing to travel
options.C: Stop referring clients altogether and attempt the procedures at the primary post
options.D: Engage community health workers to counsel and track referred clients

explanation: Community health workers can visit clients at home to address fears, answer questions, and encourage them to complete their referrals. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h8)
